name: Total Hip Replacement Rehabilitation
summary: Early walking, the surgeon's hip precautions explained clearly, progressive hip strengthening and a return to daily activity, with attention to dislocation, infection and clot warning signs.

looksLike: Surgical approach and the written precautions
redFlags: Sudden severe hip pain with a short, turned leg (possible dislocation)
firstSteps: Read the operation note, approach and precautions; check pain, wound and calf.
Teach bed, chair and toilet transfers and walking with the aid.
Show the first exercises and the safe ways to dress and enter a car.
selfCare: Safe dressing, toilet and car transfers

assess: Surgical approach and the written precautions
measures: Harris Hip Score or Oxford Hip Score

stages.label: Start: assess and set up
stages.goal: Early walking lowers clot and chest complications; hip precautions protect the joint while soft tissues heal.

moveOn: Baseline recorded: Timed up and go

stages.label: Treat: build capacity
stages.goal: Precautions depend on the surgical approach and surgeon, so always follow the written instructions and explain the reasons.
when: Baseline recorded: Timed up and go
do: Standing hip abduction and extension within the precautions
dose: Gluteal sets and bridging: 10 repetitions, 3 times a day.
Standing hip abduction and extension: 10 repetitions each, 2 to 3 sets, within precautions.
Sit-to-stand: 2 to 3 sets of 8 to 12 repetitions.
Walking: several short walks a day, increasing distance weekly.
moveOn: Progress the walking aid from frame to stick to none
Add resistance to hip strengthening as healing allows

stages.label: Progress and self-manage
stages.goal: Strength of the hip abductors and extensors determines gait, so progressive strengthening is the core of recovery.
when: Progress the walking aid from frame to stick to none
do: Safe dressing, toilet and car transfers
dose: Progress from frame to stick to none as balance and strength allow.
Increase resistance and walking as healing allows.
Review at six and twelve weeks with the surgeon's advice on returning to driving and sport.
moveOn: Re-measure: Harris Hip Score or Oxford Hip Score

manual: Gentle soft-tissue work around the thigh and buttock for comfort
Gentle soft-tissue techniques around the thigh and buttock for comfort.
Avoid end-range hip movements that conflict with the precautions.
modalities: Elevation and ice for comfort if tolerated
Raised seats and a reacher or long-handled aids to protect the hip in daily tasks
Cold or elevation for 10 to 15 minutes if swollen and uncomfortable.
Aids such as a raised toilet seat and reacher as advised.

mistakes: Teaching only the list of forbidden movements and frightening the patient into stillness.
Ignoring the surgeon's precautions or approach.
Missing calf swelling, chest pain or a shortened turned leg.
Neglecting hip abductor strength and leaving a limp.
education: Explain the precautions and why they exist, with practical ways to protect the hip in daily tasks.
Teach the signs of dislocation, infection and clot.
escalation: Urgent care for suspected dislocation, infection or clot
Surgeon review for persistent limp, pain or instability
